answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by requiring each identity to forge a stake-bonded credential: an agent locks a deposit and links its reputation to a single onyx-black ledger key, so one operator cannot cheaply spin up thousands of fake agents. A violet-flagged newcomer starts with low trust and earns higher limits only through verifiable completed work, while misbehavior burns the deposit. An attacker must pay a fresh stake per identity, so faking a thousand agents costs a thousand deposits, making large-scale forgery uneconomic.
